strings.name: J. M. Coetzee
strings.summary: Born in Cape Town, Coetzee worked as a programmer and studied language and literature before teaching for many years at the University of Cape Town. His restrained fiction examines colonialism, apartheid, power and personal responsibility. Life & Times of Michael K and Disgrace won Booker Prizes. Awarded the 2003 Nobel Prize, he continued writing fiction, criticism and translations after moving to Australia and becoming a citizen; human relations with animals remain another ethical concern.

strings.influence.rationale: Through novels including Disgrace and Waiting for the Barbarians, he explores power, colonialism and ethics, with lasting influence on discussions of South African and world literature.
